workflow: Merging multiple Excel files with different column names and data types into a single unified dataset
trigger: Weekly reporting cycle where data comes from different departments in separate Excel files
current_workaround: Manually copying and pasting columns, renaming headers, and using Excel formulas to align data types
consequence: Errors in merged data lead to incorrect reports; takes 3-4 hours every week

workflow: Automating the merging of large Excel files (100k+ rows) using pandas, but hitting memory limits and slow performance
trigger: Monthly data consolidation from multiple sources into a single analytics database
current_workaround: Splitting files into smaller chunks, merging in stages, or using SQLite as an intermediate step
consequence: Process takes over an hour and often crashes; requires manual monitoring and restarting

workflow: Merging Excel files stored in OneDrive/SharePoint without downloading them locally first
trigger: Ad-hoc requests from management to combine data from shared Excel files across teams
current_workaround: Downloading each file manually, merging locally, then re-uploading the result
consequence: Version control issues; risk of using outdated files; takes 30 minutes per request

workflow: Merging weekly inventory Excel files from multiple warehouses, each with slightly different formatting
current_workaround: Using a VBA macro that often breaks when column order changes; then manually fixing errors
consequence: Inventory discrepancies go unnoticed; takes 2 hours to fix macro issues each week

workflow: Merging monthly financial reports from different subsidiaries, each using different Excel templates
current_workaround: Hiring a temporary contractor to manually align and merge the files each month
consequence: High cost ($2k/month) and delays in reporting; errors from manual handling
